summary: Makio Ueno is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who earned a PhD from Otani University by 2009. Ueno held appointments at the Shin Buddhist Comprehensive Research Institute, Otani University, and the Otani Academic Society.

Makoto Funaoka is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology who studied at Meiji University (~1965–1977). He taught at The Open University of Japan and Komazawa University, and served at Hokkai-Gakuen University (1993–2017) as professor emeritus.

Makoto Kitada specializes in Indology and linguistics. After completing doctoral studies at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, Kitada held positions at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute and Osaka University.

Makoto Nagai (1881–1970) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned a doctorate at the University of Tokyo. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo, Nihon, Toyo, and Kamakura Women's universities, and president of Chuo Shoka Junior College.

Makoto Yoshimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who completed doctoral coursework at Waseda University. Around 2004, Yoshimura held a post as an assistant professor at Komazawa University.
Malati J. Shendge is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale, R. D. Vadekar, and Akira Hirakawa.

Malay Porey works in Indology and linguistics, completing an M.A. at Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda Educational and Research Institute (2012–2014). Porey held assistant professor posts at Durgapur Government College, Government General Degree College, Ranibandh, and Acharya Brojendra Nath Seal College.

Malcolm David Eckel is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Harvard and Oxford, working under Masatoshi Nagatomi and Daniel H. H. Ingalls, and held academic posts at Harvard, Middlebury, Michigan, Sydney, and Boston University (1990–2024).
Malcolm Huxter is a researcher in Buddhist studies who earned a B.A. (Hons) from the University of New England (1985–1991) and a Master of Psychology from Charles Sturt University (1998–2002).

Malcolm Stuart Haughton Thompson (1885–1966) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He served as principal of Government College, Rajahmundry (1931–1932) and held an appointment at SOAS University of London.
Malcolm Voyce is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who was educated at the University of London. Voyce served as a professor at Macquarie University, attested in 2009.

Mallica Kumbera Landrus is an Indologist and historian/archaeologist. As of 2026, she holds positions as Keeper of Eastern Art and Associate Professor of Indian Art at the Ashmolean Museum, affiliated with the University of Oxford and Wolfson College, Oxford.
Mamata Dash is a scholar in Indology. She completed her studies at Ravenshaw Girls' School and Utkal University.

Mamoru Tonami (1937–2024) was a scholar of Sinology, history, and Buddhist studies who studied at Kyoto University under Ichisada Miyazaki. He held faculty posts at Kyoto University (1965–2001), Kobe University (1971), and Otani University (2003).
Manabendu Banerjee is an Indologist who served as General Secretary of The Asiatic Society. He also held a post as DSA Sanskrit Co-ordinator at Jadavpur University, attested in 2003.

Manabu Asano is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued PhD studies at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, attested in 2020. Asano holds a researcher post at Minobusan University, attested in 2026.

Manasi Dilip Nadkarni works in linguistics and Indology, studying under doctoral supervisor Shyam Sundar Bhattacharya. Nadkarni is attested as a research scholar/fellow at The Asiatic Society in 2026.

Manasicha Akepiyapornchai is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed a master's at Cornell University (2014–2022). In 2022, she was appointed Assistant Professor at the University of Texas at Austin.

Mandan Mishra (1929–2001) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He held posts at the University of Rajasthan, served as Principal and Chief Editor at Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri National Sanskrit University (~1967–1989), and was Vice-Chancellor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1993–1997).

Manfred Mayrhofer (1926–2011) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Wilhelm Brandenstein at the University of Graz. He held professorships at the universities of Würzburg, Saarland, and Vienna, and served at the Austrian Academy of Sciences.
